Oscar Wilde, Lord Arthur Savile’s Crime and Other Stories.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/oscar-wilde/lord-arthur-saviles-crime-and-other-stories

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Oscar Wilde, the annotator and the author, died 1900 (Wikidata Q30875, P570 = 1900-11-30; Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oscar_Wilde).

First publication of the text used: 'Lord Arthur Savile’s Crime and Other Stories was published in 1908 by Oscar Wilde.' (SE colophon).

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1908, before 1929. Works published before 1929 entered the United States public domain by 1 January 2025, and Standard Ebooks states the same in its rights statement (below).
- Country of origin: every person whose words are in the text died in 1900 or earlier; the last to die was Oscar Wilde in 1900 (Wikidata Q30875, P570 = 1900-11-30). So the text is public domain in every country with a term of life + 100 years or less, whatever its country of first publication.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
